key_insight: AI—especially deep learning—can automate and improve the speed, consistency, and objectivity of welded-joint quality control from NDT data.
engineering_relevance: This matters for manufacturing, energy, transportation, and shipbuilding because safer and more reliable weld inspection directly affects structural integrity and maintenance decisions.
method: Systematic review of recent literature on AI-based weld quality control
Analyzed NDT modalities, defect types, datasets, and AI tasks such as detection, classification, segmentation, and prediction
Compared machine learning, CNNs, object detection/segmentation, hybrid models, and transfer learning
evidence_signal: Across recent studies, deep learning methods showed strong defect-detection and classification performance on multiple NDT data sources, with real-time inspection potential.
watch_item: Industrial deployment is still constrained by limited and imbalanced datasets, domain shift, weak generalization, and the need for explainable, standards-compliant AI.
paper_title: Artificial Intelligence in Quality Control of Welded Joints
